I am 69 years old now, and my body is not what it used to be. I have farmed this land in Quzhou County my whole life, and I only finished primary school, so I don’t read many books or follow newfangled ideas from the internet. I trust what my neighbors do and what the seed shop in town sells. This year, just like last year and the year before, I will plant **winter wheat** in the autumn and **summer maize** right after the wheat harvest. That is the only system that makes sense on the North China Plain — the soil is good, the water is there, and the buyers always come.

I have about **6 mu** of good flat land. I won’t try anything strange like vegetables or cotton because I am too old to manage the extra labor and the market risk. Wheat and maize give me steady grain to eat and sell. For the wheat, I will do **rotary tillage** before sowing in early October, and for the maize I will use **no-tillage** — I will just drill the seeds straight into the wheat stubble in mid-June. That saves my back and my diesel cost.

I will buy **improved wheat seed** (about 30 jin per mu) and **hybrid maize seed** (about 1 package per mu) from the local agro-store. Everyone uses these now; traditional seeds disappeared years ago. For fertilizer, I will put down compound fertilizer as basal and top-dress with urea. I have always done it this way. Wheat needs more care, so I will irrigate **4 times** — including the winter irrigation — and spray pesticides **4 times** (herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once). For the maize, **2 irrigations** and **3 pesticide sprays** should be enough. I expect my wheat to yield about **1,050 jin per mu** and the maize about **1,100 jin per mu**. If the weather is kind, that will feed my household and leave some grain to sell.
